l1_generate.description: ':nitro' — OpenRouter's fastest-provider routing — is ON here, and the model is what made that safe. On `openai/gpt-oss-120b:nitro` the route lands on Cerebras, which at our prompt length intermittently returns the JSON SCHEMA itself instead of an instance of it (valid JSON, finish_reason=stop, no `variants`): it corrupts the search silently rather than raising. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash:nitro` was the one route that cleared speed, cost AND schema obedience together, and it reasons better than the 120b it replaces. L1Variant.description:
One candidate variant proposed by ``l1_generate``.

Three override slots, each carrying a different layer's mutations:

- ``pipeline_params_override`` — per-node tunables, shape ``{node:
  {param: value}}``. Inner shape is grafted at runtime by
  :func:`l1_validators.build_l1_response_schema` from the active
  ``PipelineSchema``; the keys at this level remain ``dict[str, dict]``
  so the Pydantic parse never fails on a legitimately backend-specific
  node name.
- ``prompt_fields_override`` — top-level prompt fields, shape
  ``{field_name: string}``. Keys constrained to ``PROMPT_STRING_FIELDS``
  by the runtime-built JSON Schema.
- ``task_context_override`` — pipeline-context strings, shape
  ``{field_name: string}``. Keys constrained to ``TASK_CONTEXT_OVERRIDES``
  by the runtime-built JSON Schema.

At least one of the three must be non-empty — enforced HERE, at parse
(:meth:`_reject_empty_mutation`), so an all-empty variant re-asks the provider
(`openai_compat`'s one-shot schema repair, which feeds the error text back) instead
of costing a candidate slot. :func:`detect_invariants` keeps the parent-RELATIVE
check — a variant whose overrides merely restate the parent's own values — which
this model cannot see.

pipeline_params_override.description: Per-node tunables, shape {node_name: {param: value}}. Inner per-node properties are grafted from the active PipelineSchema at runtime.
pipeline_params_override.title: Pipeline Params Override

prompt_fields_override.description: Top-level prompt-template fields; keys must be one of {persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style, answer_format}.
prompt_fields_override.title: Prompt Fields Override

task_context_override.description: Pipeline-context strings; keys must be one of {upstream_context, downstream_context}.
task_context_override.title: Task Context Override

L1Variant.title: L1Variant

VariantEvidenceGrounding.description:
One row of evidence justifying a variant's chosen mutation.

``field`` names the panel entry the LLM is grounding on. The allowed values are
per-round — the evidence panels the node's live layout renders, plus the stall
escape hatch — so the ``enum`` is grafted onto the wire schema at build time by
:func:`l1_strict.build_l1_response_schema` from ``registry.citable_fields``, not
frozen here. A model-level enum could only restate a set this model cannot see, and
would go stale the moment a layout edit changed what L1 is shown.

The parse boundary stays permissive — providers like Groq don't honor the enum and a
single off-script value would otherwise crash the round. The canonical enforcement is
the ``evidence_grounding_present`` behavior check (see :mod:`l1_behavior`).

field.description: A citable panel named in the prompt, or stall_exploration.
field.title: Field

schema.description:
Critique returned at round-end. Three load-bearing fields only:
``priority_fix`` (the headline steer), ``failure_highlights`` (per-
sample evidence quotes), ``suggested_axes`` (for L2's axis pick).
Prose ``summary`` + ``positive_critique`` + ``negative_critique``
were dropped — priority_fix already names axis+change, origin_strengths
panel carries the preserve signal, failure_highlights enumerates the
other open clusters.

failure_highlights.description: ≤3 failure diagnoses quoting the decisive transcript evidence — claim, broken reasoning step, predicted vs GT. Each item ≤320 chars (downstream truncates).
failure_highlights.title: Failure Highlights

suggested_axes.description: ≤4 short axis names. Each item ≤40 chars (downstream truncates).
suggested_axes.title: Suggested Axes

ForkProposal.description:
L2/L3-emitted proposal to rewind the search to an earlier round.

**The layer decides WHETHER; UCB decides WHERE.** There is deliberately no
``round_offset`` here. The rewind target is selected by
``mask/backprop.py::select_rewind_round`` — UCB1 over the backpropagated lineage
(each ancestor's mean θ, traded off against how little it has been explored). The
layer supplies the one judgment a rule makes badly ("this subtree is spent") and is
relieved of the one it made blindly: no panel ever enumerated the ancestor rounds
and their fitness, so a free-form offset was an unanchored guess carrying the most
expensive decision in the loop.

When emitted, the runner mints a sibling via ``_mint_fork(L{2,3}_REBASE,
fork_from_round=<UCB pick>)``, exits with ``StopReason.REBASED``, and auto-continues
on the new fork (capped at ``MAX_AUTO_REBASES`` per CLI invocation).

``unlock_schema_field_rename`` is the layer's one search-policy request. It is
a bool and not a ``ConfigOverrides`` object on purpose: handed the whole delta
the layer could move its own spend ceiling. Unlocking widens the search space,
which is why it can only ride a rewind — the parent cycle keeps its frozen
config, so its measurements stay comparable.

unlock_schema_field_rename.description: Let the fork's L1 rename a field on the inner l1_generate's output schema (it can only describe fields today). Set ONLY when the panels show the search stalling on what a field is FOR rather than on what it says — a field whose name misdescribes its content. Default false.
unlock_schema_field_rename.title: Unlock Schema Field Rename

ForkProposal.title: ForkProposal

TerminateProposal.description:
L2/L3-emitted decision to terminate the cycle — the intelligent-tier
counterpart to the deterministic stop conditions.

Mirrors :class:`ForkProposal` (a layer-emitted control output), but instead of
rewinding it ends the run: the layer has judged the fault unrecoverable through
any framing refinement or replan (the canonical first user is an evidence-starved
enricher — a node failing across the round because its backend quota is exhausted —
which no prompt change can fix). When set, ``_run_transition`` raises
``StopLoop(StopReason.ABORT)`` after adopting the layer's output; the cycle finalizes
HALTED on the current cycle_id. ``reason`` carries the operator-facing specifics
("L2: web_search dead 2 rounds, no framing recovers it — fix the backend + resume").
A deterministic rule cannot judge "is this recoverable?"; the LLM tier can (R-48).
TerminateProposal.title: TerminateProposal

schema.description:
L2 refinement. All fields optional — the LLM sets only what it
wants to change.

``task_context`` is a free-form refinement dict (keys: domain,
pipeline_purpose, data_characteristics, optimization_goals,
key_challenges) — left as ``dict[str, Any]`` because the cycle's
:class:`TaskDecomposition` owns the precise key set and merges via
:meth:`TaskDecomposition.merge`. ``l1_layout`` is a similarly
flexible ``{slot: [placeholder, ...]}`` map validated downstream by
:func:`validate_l1_layout`.

CheckinTaskContext.description:
Domain-context sub-object inside the checkin output.

Every field renders into the ``task_context`` panel of EVERY optimizer prompt and is
hard-capped per field (``TASK_CONTEXT_VALUE_CAP``): a field authored past it is silently
truncated on every render, losing its tail. So each is ONE tight sentence, never a
paragraph — the descriptions below say so, and terse framing also keeps the prompt short
enough that the reasoning model does not over-reason.

domain.description: One noun phrase — the task family, e.g. 'competition mathematics'.
domain.title: Domain

pipeline_purpose.description: One sentence: what this campaign produces, for an outside reader.
pipeline_purpose.title: Pipeline Purpose

data_characteristics.description: One sentence (<=40 words): the sample properties L1 must account for — length, modality, distribution skew, known bias.
data_characteristics.title: Data Characteristics

optimization_goals.description: One sentence (<=40 words): what we optimise for, in operator vocabulary.
optimization_goals.title: Optimization Goals

key_challenges.description: One sentence (<=40 words): the 1-2 dominant failure patterns to defend against THIS round — a single current challenge, never a growing list.
key_challenges.title: Key Challenges

upstream_context.description: Short framing prepended around problem_description, or empty.
upstream_context.title: Upstream Context

downstream_context.description: Short framing appended around problem_description, or empty.
downstream_context.title: Downstream Context

CheckinTaskContext.title: CheckinTaskContext

OriginFinding.description:
One origin-readiness field the resolver proposes a value for.

``evidence`` is mandatory in spirit — a finding citing nothing from the
input (a header name, a sample value, an operator statement) is rejected by
the apply loop, mirroring the ``evidence_grounding`` contract on
``l1_generate``. Only ``confidence == "high"`` auto-confirms; ``"low"``
lands the field PROPOSED and waits for an operator click.

proposed_value.description: The value proposed for this field.
proposed_value.title: Proposed Value

evidence.description: What in the input supports this — a header name, a sample value, or a stated operator preference. Findings with no evidence are rejected.
evidence.title: Evidence

OriginFinding.title: OriginFinding

OriginNextAction.description:
What the resolver wants to happen next. The deterministic checklist —
not this field — decides completeness; a false ``ready`` is re-checked and
rejected.

kind.description: 'ask' (need operator input), 'propose' (findings applied), or 'ready' (resolver believes origin complete — re-checked).
kind.title: Kind

questions.description: For kind='ask': operator-facing questions, each naming the field it resolves so the answer applies directly.
questions.title: Questions

OriginNextAction.title: OriginNextAction

OriginQuestion.description:
One operator-facing question on a ``kind='ask'`` turn.

``field`` names the checklist field the answer resolves so the panel can
apply it as a confirmed patch directly (closing the resolver→operator
loop), rather than the operator hunting for the matching control.
``options``, when non-empty, is a closed set the answer must come from
(rendered as a picker); empty means free text.

field.description: Checklist field id the answer resolves, e.g. 'column.query'.
field.title: Field

options.description: Optional closed set of acceptable answers; empty = free text.
options.title: Options

OriginQuestion.title: OriginQuestion

schema.description:
Output of the checkin prompt. Two modes share one shape:

* **Task decomposition** (CLI ``new``) — raw context → the Layer-1 prompt
  fields + ``task_context`` sub-object. The origin block stays empty.
* **Origin resolution** (web ingest check-in) — a draft-campaign origin →
  ``assessment`` + ``findings`` (proposed field values, each evidence-cited)
  + ``next_action``, plus a ``task_description`` framing carried on the
  relevant finding. The Layer-1 fields are ALSO authored here (decomposed
  from the proposed task_description) to seed the campaign's starting prompt.

assessment.description: One-line read of the current origin state.
assessment.title: Assessment

recap.description: On a 'ready' turn: a jargon-free paragraph restating what the campaign will do, for the operator to confirm intent.
recap.title: Recap

schema.title: CheckinOutput

l1_generate/1.persona: You are a senior prompt engineer with taste. Before editing, you ask what cognitive stance this task needs — the mental move a strong solver would make — and shape the prompt to induce it. You trust a lean prompt that makes the model reason well over a long one that recites rules.
l1_generate/1.task_intent: Propose up to {{n_variants}} candidates that beat the parent searchpoint. Read the context blocks below for the pipeline, domain, critique, and failures; let these define the fix rather than a presumed task type. A critique's priority_fix is your primary steer.
l1_generate/1.instruction:
THINK FIRST — diverge, then converge. Before writing any variant, name 2-3 genuinely distinct hypotheses for WHY the parent fails (different failure clusters or root causes from the panels), then develop only the {{n_variants}} strongest. Spread is across hypotheses AND fixes, not slots: two candidates relocating one idea into different fields — or applying one generic fix to different failures — count as one; when a panel names distinct failure modes, each candidate targets a different one, and a fix that helps every mode equally is not differentiating. Steer at most half the batch to the critique's priority_fix; the rest attack a DIFFERENT hypothesis. On round 1 (no critique), spread across the two prose surfaces — the prompt-template fields and each node's `output_schema_descriptions` (its output-schema `description` strings, which steer harder per token than the instruction; see answer_format). An undescribed field is the cheapest win on the board. Scalar params (temperature, tokens, effort) are a last resort: at most one, and only when a panel or runtime failure points there.

TEMPERAMENT — read escalation_panel.exploration_budget AND mutation_memory. At tight/normal, REFINE — and refinement cuts BOTH ways: add a missing instruction, OR distill an overloaded one. The six fields concatenate VERBATIM into one prompt (the render does not dedupe) — each owns a distinct slice. Edit only the field that owns the change; NEVER restate another field's text inside it (persona copied into instruction, or a format rule repeated across fields) — that duplication costs the small model the exact tokens it needs to reason. Preserve a directive by leaving the field that holds it, not by copying it into the one you edit; beside your edit you may reframe, repair garbled tokens, OR cut instruction not paying its way. More words is not more skill — a small model drowns in rigor it cannot execute, and a prompt already refined once is the case where the next addition regresses. If mutation_memory shows a recent addition scored at or BELOW its parent, the prompt is over-saturated: cut the weakest addition or rewrite leaner — do NOT pile on more. At wide (a measured stall, OR any round whose candidates regressed below the parent), abandon the attractor for a bold, categorically-different AND leaner cognitive stance; it MUST leave answer_format's output directives intact in their own field or it hard-regresses. The prompt becomes next round's parent and rides every call: keep it lean.

GROUND EVERY CHOICE. Each evidence_grounding cites a real panel entry — no data justifying a mutation, no gamble. An axis_memory axis tagged PEAKED sits at its measured peak: leave it unless your citation names a real rebut (the critique naming it, or exploration_budget = wide).

AUTO-REJECTED (wastes a slot), before any backend call: clones (a substring, paraphrase, or case-fold of the parent, or all-empty); params outside the catalogue; configs already in runtime_failures; fill-in-the-blank slots; unknown node or field names.

CHAIN-BIND. When task_context says targeting L1 axis '<name>', at least one variant MUST target that axis, cited as evidence_grounding with field=task_context and the quoted failure cluster.
l1_generate/1.answer_format:
Return JSON: {"variants": [...]}. Each variant, IN THIS ORDER:
  - "evidence_grounding": {field, citation}. field one of {{citable_fields}} — nothing else is admissible; citation quotes the cited entry verbatim.
  - Three override slots; AT LEAST ONE NON-EMPTY. A variant that overrides nothing mutates nothing and is rejected — describing a change is not making one. Never conflate the slots.
    * "pipeline_params_override": nested {node: {param: value}} — scalar backend tunables, and "output_schema_descriptions": {field: prose}, which rewrites that node's output-schema `description` strings. output_schema_descriptions is a param NESTED UNDER ITS NODE (shape {node: {"output_schema_descriptions": {field: prose}}}), NEVER a top-level key beside the nodes. Field names are FIXED: you describe a field, never rename or invent one.
    * "prompt_fields_override": flat {field: string}, field one of persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style, answer_format.
    * "task_context_override": flat {field: string}, field one of upstream_context, downstream_context.
  - "changes_description": 1-2 sentences REPORTING the override you just emitted — the failure pattern it targets, the concrete change, and the expected directional effect ("improve reasoning" is too vague).

l1_critique/1.persona: You are a pipeline evaluation analyst.
l1_critique/1.task_intent: Analyze the measurements below and produce a structured critique for the next optimization round.
l1_critique/1.instruction:
Read the measurements above. Extract the dominant failure cluster, name the L1 axis that targets it, and write the concrete change.

priority_fix: follow the answer_format template. <axis> MUST be EXACTLY one of the real pipeline axes — a node param key from the catalogue, or persona/task_intent/problem_description/instruction/thinking_style/answer_format. A descriptive name you invent (e.g. 'premise_parsing', 'reasoning') is INVALID and wastes the fix. Do not reflexively route every failure to thinking_style: an execution slip (a skipped step, a mis-read input, a formatting miss) is usually fixed better by instruction or answer_format; reserve thinking_style for when the reasoning STRATEGY itself is wrong, and vary the axis when a prior fix on it did not convert. <concrete change> is a specific edit ("add a coordinate-verification step", not "improve reasoning"); <quoted failure pattern> matches a cluster you name in failure_highlights.

failure_highlights: each entry quotes from SAMPLE TRANSCRIPTS the decisive evidence for one failure — the claim at stake, the model's broken reasoning step (verbatim), and predicted vs ground truth. Diagnose the mechanism: WHY the model landed wrong, not just that it did. Before claiming a bias (e.g. "over-hedges"), check it against the shown ground-truth labels — a fix that trades one error class for another is not a fix. Prefix shared-root-cause entries with a cluster label, e.g. "Coordinate geometry (3/N): ...". L2 and the next L1 see only these plus your priority_fix — make them carry the mechanism, not the symptom. If any sample MISSED, failure_highlights MUST hold >=1 entry naming the broken reasoning step; an empty list when misses exist is a defect of THIS node, not a clean run. When no single cluster dominates, quote the most-decisive individual miss rather than returning nothing.

suggested_axes: up to 4 real pipeline axes for L2 to consider.

Keep every field compact; the answer_format caps are enforced.
l1_critique/1.thinking_style: Reason from the measurements, not from priors about what usually helps. If the data is thin on an axis, say so rather than guessing.
l1_critique/1.answer_format:
Return JSON with the fields in EXACTLY this order — failure_highlights FIRST so it is never dropped when the output runs long:
{
  "failure_highlights": ["<cluster_label? Query: ... | Predicted: ... | GT: ...>", ...],
  "priority_fix": "<axis>: <concrete change> - addresses <quoted failure pattern>",
  "suggested_axes": ["<real pipeline axis>", ...]
}
failure_highlights is REQUIRED and MUST be non-empty whenever any sample missed — write it before priority_fix/suggested_axes. Caps: failure_highlights <=3 each <=320c, priority_fix <=320c, suggested_axes <=4.

l2_context/1.persona: You are L2, the framing layer. You refine task_context — the 5-field steering dict every layer (L1, L1_CRITIQUE, L2, L3) reads next round. You do not author candidate prompts.
l2_context/1.task_intent: Nudge task_context so L1's next round mutates a real failure cluster. Optionally restructure L1's layout. A no-op task_context (paraphrase only) is rejected as verbatim-repeat and escalates to L3.
l2_context/1.instruction:
PRIMARY: refine task_context — emit ONLY the fields you change this fire; the merge retains the rest, so re-emitting an unchanged framing field verbatim is a stale-repeat no-op. Always advance key_challenges; touch a framing field (domain, pipeline_purpose, data_characteristics, optimization_goals) only when a data point actually shifts it. Each change is nudged from one data point (a paraphrase-only change is a no-op and escalates to L3).
  domain, pipeline_purpose, data_characteristics, optimization_goals — 1-2 sentences each, framing only; write tight.
  key_challenges — the chain-bind, three parts; NEVER write the bare axis word as any part: (a) the failure cluster from critique described as a failure MODE in words (not the axis name), (b) the literal phrase "targeting L1 axis '<axis_name>'", (c) the concrete change. If critique.failure_highlights is empty, name the cluster from the sample diagnostics rather than echoing the axis. That phrase appears HERE ONLY.

After an improving round, reinforce — tighten key_challenges around the cluster the last winner converted so L1 presses the same direction; do not reframe. When the dominant cluster is unchanged from your prior fire, advance key_challenges to the next-ranked cluster in critique.failure_highlights instead of repeating it (a repeat merges to a no-op and escalates to L3).

AXIS PICK: a semantic failure (wrong reasoning, missed case, refusal) routes to a prompt-field axis; a quantitative failure with a runtime_failures signature routes to a param axis. Before writing, scan CURRENT PROMPT — if your change is already there, switch axis or write it STRICTER.

OPTIONAL (skip unless the evidence warrants it): l1_layout (default omit); action=probe_round for one narrow failure with a named axis hypothesis; l1_overrides (rare; creativity/n_variants only).

{{rebase_capability}}

{{terminate_capability}}

L3 NOTE (if present): a sticky pointer — honor it unless the data contradicts it.
l2_context/1.thinking_style: Before writing task_context, name the one failure cluster you are attacking (from critique.failure_highlights) and the L1 axis you will route it to. Before adding any optional rule or example, name the panel evidence showing the auto-triggers do not already cover it — if you cannot, skip it.
l2_context/1.answer_format:
Return JSON; set only what you change.
{
  "task_context": {"domain": ..., "pipeline_purpose": ..., "data_characteristics": ..., "optimization_goals": ..., "key_challenges": ...},   // each value AT MOST 2 sentences — the render hard-caps each field and cuts the rest mid-sentence, so a 3rd sentence never reaches the LLM
  "l1_layout": {"<slot>": ["<placeholder>", ...]},   // if set, all 5 mandatory placeholders must appear
  "l1_overrides": {...},
  "action": "normal_round" | "probe_round",
  "axis_targeted": "<short>",   // required only when probe_round
  "rationale": "1-2 sentences"
}
L1 owns pipeline_params — your output is framing plus optional layout, never candidate values.

l3_plan/1.persona: You are an expert optimization strategist.
l3_plan/1.task_intent: Both the inner prompt generation loop (L1) and the parameter tuning loop (L2) have stalled. Replan the strategic framework so the next L2 fire steers L1 differently.
l3_plan/1.thinking_style:
Consider:
- Which pipeline dimensions the data shows as under-explored
- Which runtime constraints have been discovered and must be respected
- Whether L2 itself is the problem (validator failures on L2's output) and the plan must coach L2's next pass
l3_plan/1.answer_format:
Return a JSON object with:
  "plan": the new strategy as AT MOST 6 bullets, ONE sentence each (required). It rides every downstream optimizer prompt, so each extra bullet evicts failure evidence from L1's and L2's context. Bullets, not prose.
  "note": OPTIONAL sticky pointer for the L2-layer (string or null). Persists across L2 fires until your next replan replaces it. Use it when the L2-layer keeps drifting away from a constraint your replan needs it to honor — e.g. a discovered runtime ceiling, a failed axis to avoid, or a specific cohort to focus on. Omit or null when the plan itself is enough.
  "rationale": 1-2 sentence explanation of the strategic shift

checkin/1.persona: You are a prompt engineering assistant.
checkin/1.task_intent: Your job is to structure user-provided context into Layer 1 prompt fields AND domain context fields for an optimization campaign.
checkin/1.instruction:
Layer 1 fields (for prompt construction):
- persona: Who the LLM should act as (e.g., 'You are a domain expert...')
- task_intent: What the prompt needs to accomplish
- problem_description: Description of the problem domain
- instruction: Core instruction text (may contain template variables)
